summary.description: Chloroalkanes are short-chain chlorinated paraffins consisting of carbon, hydrogen, and chlorine. They are typically yellowish oily liquids with a faint odour and are used mainly in industrial metalworking fluids for cutting, drilling, and machining metals.
emission_sources: Use of chloroalkanes as metal cutting fluids
environmental_impact: Toxic to aquatic life and bio-accumulate in marine and freshwater species
Persistent in the environment due to lack of biodegradability
Potential carcinogenic effects and harmful impacts on kidneys, liver, and thyroid from high exposure

top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: Chloroalkanes are highly toxic to aquatic organisms and bio-accumulate in marine and freshwater life, disrupting aquatic ecosystems and food chains.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Persistence and bioaccumulation of chloroalkanes threaten freshwater quality, affecting access to safe and clean water.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Potential carcinogenic effects and damage to liver, kidneys, and thyroid from high exposure pose risks to human health.
